Toys & models

10 aviation gift ideas for older kids who love planes

Older children may want to build, collect, draw, or understand how aviation works. The most useful gift follows that curiosity rather than assuming every airplane fan wants the same remote-controlled toy. This shortlist spans creative projects, learning activities, and experiences to choose with a caregiver.

By Pilot Gift Guide Updated 2026-10-20

How we choose our recommendations
In this guideThe ideasHow to chooseMore gift ideas

The ideas

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    Aircraft building set

    Choose a manageable challenge in a theme they like. Check the finished size and whether a parent wants another permanent display model.

  2. 2

    Illustrated aviation encyclopedia

    Pick an edition with readable diagrams and captions. Browse sample pages to judge whether the text invites curiosity or feels like homework.

  3. 3

    Paper-airplane activity book

    Give materials and room to experiment together. Favor a book with clear folding steps over promises about extraordinary flight performance.

  4. 4

    Snap-fit model kit

    Confirm the assembly method and recommended age. Some kits still involve delicate parts, even when glue or paint is not required.

  5. 5

    Aircraft drawing supplies

    Pair a sketchbook with suitable pencils and reference pictures. This works especially well for a child already drawing wings, liveries, and airport scenes.

  6. 6

    Museum scavenger activity

    Create a short list of things to notice during a visit. Keep it flexible so the child can spend time on unexpected favorites.

  7. 7

    Airport-themed board game

    Check playing age, game length, and the number of people needed. A theme cannot rescue a game that nobody at home wants to play.

  8. 8

    Beginner photography outing

    Use an existing camera or phone from a permitted viewing location. The gift can be time, attention, and printing a favorite image afterward.

  9. 9

    Airline history scrapbook

    Gather postcards and pictures for a creative project. Let the child organize it their way rather than imposing an adult collector’s system.

  10. 10

    Introductory simulator session

    Choose an age-appropriate setup with caregiver involvement. Treat it as an activity to enjoy, with no claim that it provides flight qualifications.

How to choose

Start with what the child already enjoys doing independently. Check age guidance, required supervision, tools, and batteries for each product. Avoid expensive hobby equipment until you know whether the interest is building, operating, collecting, or simply learning more about aircraft.

Prices and availability can change. Check the exact model, delivered total and return terms with the seller. Our recommendations are researched editorial selections, not hands-on test results.
